purpose: Names for the per-slot part INDEX in a save-file part ID. Part IDs decode as <partset><index>, where <partset> is normally the car's own ordinal (shared components use a donor set, e.g. transmission 2102000 on both ord 2866 and 3852). The index is NOT the tile position in that car's menu -- it is a position in a GLOBAL per-slot vocabulary, and each car's menu shows only the subset it offers, in ascending index order. One map therefore names parts for every car; no per-car upgrade-menu capture is needed for the tier slots.

evidence.refutes_menu_position: 1992 Honda NSX-R (ord 412): docs/fh6-ui-spec.md 2.2 records the 'Front Anti-roll Bars' menu with exactly TWO tiles (Stock, Race), yet the decoded front_arb index is 3. A tile position cannot be 3 in a 2-tile menu.
supports_global_vocabulary: brakes / front_arb / rear_arb take exactly {0,1,2,3} across all 163 cars -- a 4-value vocabulary, not a per-car list length.
springs_dampers takes exactly {0..5}. The NSX-R menu lists 4 tiles in the order Stock, Race, Rally, Drift = indexes {0,3,4,5}; the decoded set for ord 412 is {0,3,5}, a subset, and ascending.
brakes on the NSX-R lists 3 tiles Stock, Sport, Race = {0,2,3}; decoded set for ord 412 is {0,3}, a subset.
The spec's own naming pattern (section 5.7) is a global vocabulary: Stock / Sport / Race / Rally / Drift / Offroad.

confidence_key.verified: name read verbatim off a named frame AND its index position confirmed by the ascending-subset test
confidence_key.inferred: position follows from the confirmed neighbours and the standard vocabulary, but no frame names it

tier_slots._note: Global vocabulary. Index means the same thing on every car.
tier_slots._star: A trailing * marks an inferred name. Tier 2 = Sport and tier 3 = Race are now READ VERBATIM from the in-game basket (2026-09-01): 'Sport Cams and Valves', 'Sport Weight Reduction', 'Race Exhaust', 'Race Front Anti-roll Bars'. Only tier 1 remains unnamed.
tier_slots._index0_warning: A decoded index of 0 is NOT yet trustworthy -- see validation.open_anomaly. name_part() still returns 'Stock' for it; callers that need certainty should check the index is >= 1.

catalogue_slots._note: The index is still global-positional, but the ITEM at each position is car-specific (donor engines, brand wings, rim styles, body kits). These need the car's own list -- data/engine-swaps.json already covers engines.

unresolved.observation: These take {0..N} union {100..10N} union {200..} union {300..} -- a second dimension in the hundreds digit, not a flat tier. The spec notes the Front Tire Width grid grew from 4 to 7 tiles after the widebody/rim change, so the hundreds digit most likely selects the body/conversion variant the part belongs to. NOT yet confirmed; do not name these from the tier table.

validation.unlock_gating_test: docs/fh6-ui-spec.md 5.8: Race/Rally/Drift springs unlock SPRING, DAMPER AND ALIGNMENT tuning; Stock/Street/Sport leave it locked. Damping default is 10.5 (the ONLY front_bump value at indexes 1 and 2, n=12). Across 531 tunes: index 3/4/5 = 100.0% moved off default (n=275, zero exceptions); index 1/2 = 0.0% (n=12). Both ends match the gating exactly, which is what confirms 3=Race, 4=Rally, 5=Drift and that 1,2 sit below the unlock.
validation.open_anomaly: index 0 splits 103 at default / 142 tuned, where the gating predicts ~0% tuned. The two sets are DISJOINT BY CAR (49 cars vs 54 cars, zero overlap), so this is a property of the car, not of the tune -- i.e. the <partset><index> split is not yet reliable for every ordinal, most likely a prefix ambiguity where another partset's ID starts with this car's ordinal digits. Until that is resolved, treat a decoded index of 0 as UNRELIABLE and do not name it; indexes 1-5 are sound.
validation.counter_evidence_noted: Within index 0, the default-damping group is mostly Race ARB (87) while the tuned group is mostly Stock ARB (124) -- backwards from what a genuinely-upgraded car would show, which is further reason to distrust the index-0 bucket rather than to reinterpret index 0 as a non-stock part.

index_is_dense_or_sparse.finding: Two different index schemes share the same field, and confusing them sends a clone to the wrong tile.

sparse_global_ladder.rule: Index is a position in a GLOBAL vocabulary; each car exposes only the subset it offers, ascending. So the index can exceed the tile count -- the NSX-R's 2-tile Front Anti-roll Bars menu decodes to index 3 (Race).
sparse_global_ladder.implication: Match by NAME (Race/Rally/Drift), never by counting tiles.

dense_per_car_list.rule: Conversions are per-car lists, so the index IS the tile position, 0-based. Verified on camera 2026-09-01: the NSX-R Drivetrain Swap menu has exactly 2 tiles (Stock INSTALLED, AWD OWNED) and the target's drivetrain index is 1 = the 2nd tile.
dense_per_car_list.implication: Match by POSITION for these three.

aspiration_is_two_steps.finding: Forced induction is a CONVERSION plus a TIER, bought in two different menus.
aspiration_is_two_steps.step_1: Body Kits and Conversions > Aspiration  picks the TYPE (turbo / centrifugal / roots).
aspiration_is_two_steps.step_2: Upgrade Shop > Engine > <that type>  sells the TIER.
aspiration_is_two_steps.save_encoding: The save stores only the tier, in the slot NAMED for the type -- so the TYPE is encoded by WHICH of single_turbo / twin_turbo / quad_turbo / centrifugal_supercharger / pos_supercharger is populated. That is why the slot literally called 'aspiration' is empty in all 532 tunes; it is not a phantom label, it is a menu with no separate stored value.
aspiration_is_two_steps.verified: 2026-09-01, forzahorizon6_XtE0aSrdbE.mp4 frame 090: on the stock block with no aspiration conversion fitted, the Engine menu shows EIGHT tiles and no supercharger sub-menu. The spec's post-swap capture of the same menu had ELEVEN. The tier cannot be bought until the conversion is installed.
aspiration_is_two_steps.cost_of_getting_it_wrong: A clone route that lists the supercharger under Engine sends you to a menu where it does not exist.

names_read_from_basket_2026_09_01.source: Basket Items screen, 1992 Honda NSX-R, 19 items, total CR 35,600. Names are verbatim.

names_read_from_basket_2026_09_01.transmission_index_is_gear_count: Index 7 renders as 'Race Transmission: 7 Speed'. The transmission index is the SPEED COUNT, not a tier position -- so it must never be read against the Stock/Sport/Race ladder.
names_read_from_basket_2026_09_01.cams_and_valves_are_one_part: The shop sells 'Sport Cams and Valves' as a SINGLE item, yet the save carries separate camshaft and valves slots, and in this target they differ (camshaft idx 2, valves idx 0). Either the slot we call 'valves' is mislabelled, or one part writes two slots unequally. UNRESOLVED -- do not name the 'valves' slot until this is settled.
names_read_from_basket_2026_09_01.rear_wing_is_dense: The NSX-R Rear Wing menu has 3 tiles (Honda stock / Rocket Bunny - Race / Forza Horizon 6 - Race) and this car's four tunes use indexes 0, 1 and 2 -- all three present, so the index IS the 0-based tile position. idx 2 = the Forza wing, NOT the Rocket Bunny one.
